title: robocraft
text: TL;DR: Game is fun. Game is balanced. New content all the time. Its like Lego + World of Tanks except cool. To summarize Robocraft: there are 2-3 main aspects of the gameplay in Robocraft. Firstly, you need to build your vehicle(s) which is done in a 3D grid system with all main chassis components being 1x1x1 cubes and then attaching necessary weapons and movement devices. Secondly, you play! You get match made into a match against players of roughly the same tech level as you, with no compensation for player skill. Controls are standard for a driving game, and there is a variety of asymmetric maps with different sets of terrain that favor different vehicles and different tactics. The map is chosen randomly, your best chance is to design something that works well on ALL maps as opposed to one in particuilar. Third and finally, you unlock and purchase (using F2P or P2P currency) more parts. Due to the need to unlock new parts and upgrade your bot to proceed to unlock more new parts, it can be prohibitively expensive to get everything, and you may need to focus, and after a while you'll find it takes a while to get to the next tier. Although this isn't necessarily part of the gameplay it's nonetheless a very big part of the game, and it directly dictates how you play the game. After all, you can't make an airplane or a walker if you don't get the parts. Reasons Why It Works Large variety of parts and a large number of effective ways to build your robot ensure lots of variety, and attentive developers as well as the release of new content keeps the metagame flowing so it never gets too stale. Gameplay tiers are defined by robot ranking. Each component directly adds its robot ranking to your total. Robot ranking, the maximum robot ranking per tier, and in general the health pool of each block and damage of each weapon increase exponentially with each tier. What this means is that within a tier, you're allowed to use a fairly large amount of  components from within that tier, but only a few from higher tiers, otherwise you end up pushing yourself into the next tier. Similarly you can use a very large amount of components from lower tiers, although this is often undesirable. This prevents you from getting completely smashed by someone who has better components than you. Problems There are a few balance sweet spots and plenty of times you will go up against robots that are UNFAIRLY strong, and in some cases will have no real way to deal with them, other than to radically change your robot, and sometimes you will be forced to conform in order to win. Nerfs are sometimes given out rather heavy handedly which has overreaching effects due to the variety of ways components can be used. Ultimately these nerfs are for the good of the game but sometimes that means cool, unique and creative bot designs become completely unviable because a more competitie use of the parts required them to be nerfed. For instance headlights, as seemingly harmless and functionally cosmetic component had a significant limit put on the number you can use because their overuse was detrimental to players on older computers and this was being used for a competitive advantage. The difficulty and time involved in creating a functioning, viable and fun robot is too much for some people, which results in them simply copying the most common design, leading to games being flooded with 3 types of bots when there are theoretically ENDLESS bots that can be made, and I fear as the community gets larger this "follow the leader" approach will only become more and more pronounced. Ultimately though I find the game very fun inspite of all that as to me, it's simply an excuse to vary my bot design and strive harder to craft something that can break the meta.

text: The best 11$ you could spend on a game. A game with a very simple premise: throw dodgeballs at other people (or bots). There are many varied levels for all styles of play and many different game modes. Don't like the default game modes? Make your own! The game creator is easy to use and you can make some pretty "interesting" game modes (super fast players with massive super-bouncy-laser balls). Not much to talk about in terms of graphics, they're minimalist, and in this case it works very well. Also worth mentioning that I don't think i've ever run into a single bug. For 11$, this game is jam-packed with features that make it worth easily 25$, maybe 30$. My only complaint is with regards to the items system and bot behaviour. If you're unaware, you get items at certain time intervals and you can combine 5 basic items to make an advanced item, and 5 advanced items to make cosmetic items. The basic items are gears, springs, bolts, nuts, and screws. I have 0 gears and about 15 of each other item, so i'm not sure if i'm just really unlucky or if the item drops need rebalancing but either way it's pretty frustrating. Bots can be pretty cheap too at times by catching balls from behind their backs or having perfect aim and perfect compensation for movement from the other side of the arena, even on medium difficulty. Despite that though, the game is a ridiculous amount of fun and is constantly being updated. There's some other features i've left out (like being able to add your own music) but I think i've explained enough why this is worth a buy. I definitely recommend picking this up for $10.99! And if you have some friends, pick up four copies for $27.99 (a massive deal if you ask me).

title: rochard
text: It was the Space Debris music in the trailer that sold this game to me. So having just bought the Soundtrack Edition of the game, I listened through the soundtrack first before playing the game. Yes, Space Debris is such a great track, but the rest of the soundtrack certainly didn't disappoint either; from the '90's 'Independence Day' feel of John's Theme, to the excellent Tangerine Dream techno-ambience of The Fight, the Rochard OST is so enjoyable from start to finish..........so what about the game itself? Rochard is a light-hearted physics-based side scroller set in a future-grunge world of space mining. Playing as John Rochard, you use your grapple gun and anti-grav physics to overcome environmental obstacles and enemies. The production of Rochard is top-notch and the physics superbly done. The game starts off easy enough and the first couple of levels act as tutorials easing the player into the physic-based system of the game. It's too early for me to say how the game pans out, but I think it's hardly going to disappoint from what I've experienced so far. Great characters and enjoyable cut-scenes, I'm genuinely looking forward to spending more time with John Rochard & friends. Edit: As it turned out, Rochard was an immensely enjoyable game from start to finish. The game was lean with no padding. Checkpoints were frequent and positioned so there was rarely any grind to get a previous position after dying. The length of the game was also satisfying, never threatening to outstay its welcome. Playing with a PS3 controller (360 mapped), the controls were very responsive and satisfying. There was also a good balance between combat and physics-based puzzles. There are Gold badges to collect throughout the game. They don't contribute to any weapon upgrades, etc, but are positioned in the levels to add extra challenge for the obsessive collector. After beating the game, I find I can select individual levels to find badges I've missed which adds to the replay value. I'll probably enjoy playing through Rochard a couple of more times whilst patiently waiting for Episode II. Addictive gameplay, tight controls, challenging puzzles (never too hard), varied combat, collectables, cute characters with a great central eponymous hero: 9/10.

title: rochard
text: A very short review after just over an hour of play. More to follow, but I want players to know about this game while it's still SO cheap. Amazing graphics, pretty good story, great voice acting, stellar music. This is a thinking player's game, heavily involving physics. Gravity, and gravity control is a big part of this game, and so far using gravity to place and throw objects is used instead of traditional weapons. I must say, squashing bad guys with huge, heavy boxes, or grav-throwing explosives at them is FAR more satisfying than just....."bang". (Nothing wrong with "bang". I LIKE "bang".) And to grab an errant robot with a gravity beam, then smash it rapidly against opposing walls is oddly....calming. If you typically avoid platformers, or like me, buy them expecting to fail, "rochard" may be your solution. Many, if not most, of the multitudinous puzzles seem to have more than one solution. One, the typical "brute force" sort, but also a much easier, more "scientific" one. Very good learning curve. Short, reasonable checkpoint intervals. AND a hero who looks and sounds much like so many of us! MOST importantly, this game is really a LOT of fuN! If PORTAL was a platformer, it just might be "rochard". At this price, WHILE it's this price, you owe it to yourself to at least take a look at the Store Page. What's to lose? $1.49 is all! ($2.09 with soundtrack & artbook.) At this price I have to give the HIGHEST possible recommendation.

title: rock of ages
text: You send a boulder down a twisty slope towards your opponent’s castle, steering and jumping--don’t ask how--as you splat flat buildings and little screaming people, bouncing over defences and smacking into the gates. At the same time, your opponent (computer or human) does the same to you. After the rock bashes a chunk off the gate workers start carving another boulder and, in the brief downtime, you place defences like explosives, wind machines, brave doomed elephants and cows. It's more meticulous than I expected. When I'm building traps I'm being rushed, but when racing downhill I'm constantly made to slow down. Still, there's nothing quite like it. The animation, which goes through various periods of art history as you progress, is gorgeous and hilarious. The boss battles aren’t a great addition, although defeating Michelangelo’s David by shooting a boulder at his♥♥♥♥♥♥was certainly an experience.

title: rocketbirds: hardboiled chicken
text: Completed in 5 hours. Not a bad game. Actually, I'd recommend it as a good action platformer (with some unfortunate puzzle elements). However: the areas with waves of enemies in a locked room are broken, with enemies being "human" (penguin) shields to your bullets but not to each others. I kept getting killed by enemies that were behind other enemies who could shoot past their allies but I was instead shooting the dead, juggled bodies of their allies instead of them. Also, the jetpack sections are a mess, with a huge zoom-out effect and screen scroll every time new flying enemies appear, making it harder to see the ammo or health pickup you were aiming for or the rocket that is still chasing you (fired from a previous enemy) that you're still expected to avoid, even if both you and the rocket are off screen. Both the waves of enemies and the jetpack sections checkpoint frequently, so they become a battle of attrition rather than skill. These two sections are also where the game showcases its' soundtrack. Short sections of uninspired music looping endlessly. On first hearing at the title screen, it got me in the mood for an action game. But repetitively looped in frustrating, cheaply designed action sequences (the waves and the jetpack), both these sections and the one to two verse or chorus songs had both gameplay and music making each other worse. There are also some ridiculous puzzle sections involving playing around with box stacking and elevators that do nothing but artificially lengthen the game. One section had me chase an enemy up a set of elevators, back down, and then back up again, requiring a floor change at each of about six floors on the first two of those runs. I was not amused. Other than the above, quite an enjoyable game. But if the come out with a sequel, I will not be buying it, given the amount of cheap time-lengthening and unbalanced gameplay of this game. That, and the story of "Rocketbirds: Hardboilded Chicken" (what there is of it) would hardly support two or more games. I doubt I'll play this game again, because there's no way I'm putting up with that nonsense again. Oh, and if you get stuck on how to proceed, like I did numerous times (minor SPOILERS), the answer is ALWAYS one of: run past it, use one or more crates, or control an enemy through brain bugs. Don't expect the puzzles to be deep, or you'll just end up confused.
